gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histologically confirmed solid tumor for which regorafenib is an approved treatment (e.g., metastatic colorectal cancer, gastrointestinal stromal tumor, hepatocellular carcinoma, glioblastoma, or others)

candidate_evidence.quote: This study aims to evaluate whether a combination of oral zinc supplementation and transdermal clobetasol cream is effective in preventing and reducing the severity of hand-foot skin reaction (HFSR) induced by regorafenib treatment.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Initiating regorafenib treatment for the first time

role_evidence.quote: This intervention aims to evaluate the effect of zinc in preventing and reducing the severity of regorafenib-induced hand-foot skin reaction (HFSR).
This intervention aims to assess the efficacy of clobetasol in preventing regorafenib-induced HFSR.
Initiating regorafenib treatment for the first time

coder_notes: Supportive-care study (prevention of regorafenib-induced hand-foot skin reaction) in a multi-tumour population with glioblastoma named in inclusion. Regorafenib is not a registered intervention but every patient starts it, so listed as soc_backbone (background). Zinc is a dietary supplement and clobetasol a topical steroid, both supportive. Three experimental arms compare prophylaxis strategies; none functions as a control, so control_arm_from_other_arms = no. Treatment setting for GBM not stated.
